Celmaldor (Z22)

Survey-table region: Wescann / Gerudia.

In brief: Restore a declining Moon Elf port to the northern sea lanes and turn a merchant-dominated republic into a silver-white alliance spanning peoples and oceans.

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 75/100 | Autocracy 45/100 | Magic–Artifice 18/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 83/100) | Pluralism 88/100. The profile changes from merchant oligarchy and the old colonial order (Autocracy 65, Pluralism 55) to a reformed Silver Alliance (Autocracy 45, Pluralism 88).

The v2.1 values score is Good (76/100), with an improving trajectory: merchant private armies and extraction of colonial wealth (Neutral 52/100) → civic rights and overseas autonomy reforms (Good 76/100).

Story: High | Mission-tree length: Long (48 exclusive missions) | Mission-tree update: Base mod v1.37.5.0; exact rework date unverified | Distinctiveness: High | Tedium: Medium | Early pressure: Medium | Expansion: Upper-medium.

A northern port built by wanderers

Celmaldor is an existing Moon Elf republic in 1444. The country and its capital share a name, and Blue Reachmen are accepted as a cultural member. The history script describes ruler Thaelarel Icewind as tolerant and just, but cowardly. Adshaw and Bevike are historic rivals, while Celmaldor leads the Reach League. This is not a late-game Tag formed by another country: its port, merchant families, and league already define the opening state.【Local history script】

The offline English History of the Principality of Celmaldor says the navigator Maldorian captained the Remnant Fleet's Migrant Ship Whitespear. He supported Munas Moonsinger's eastward voyage but refused to join the later War of the Sorcerer-King. Maldorian and his followers sailed along the Cannorian coast and settled in the Alenic Reach in 1002, founding Celmaldor. The Wiki says the new city-state expanded through diplomacy and force, integrated or subjugated neighbours, seized Deland and Mawdock, and vassalised the Serpentgarder; Whiteharbor was built to hold the Remnant Fleet. These are Wiki backstory claims, not an account of the current 1444 government, which is established by the local republic history script.【Wiki】【Local history script】

Past grandeur does not mean present strength. Mission text says Whiteharbor lies idle, while pirates and northern raiders threaten trade routes. Merchant families—the White Spear, Icewind, and Frosttide—control private armies, leaving the republic's regular forces unable to act independently. The gnomish Storm Isles nearby are also outside Celmaldor's control. The player must secure the straits and treasury before restoring sea power.【Local narrative text】

A mission tree about who shares prosperity

The current Celmaldor_Missions.txt contains 48 Z22-exclusive missions. Structured queries may also include two generic missions; those do not make the exclusive tree a 50-mission tree. Early objectives begin with “Defend Our Reach,” restore Whiteharbor, and break the merchant families' private armies. Later, the Silver Alliance is made attractive to new members, allies receive investment, the rivalry with Bevike is addressed, and commercial magic and artificery are put to productive use. Artifice does not run the economy from day one; it becomes a new industry through relevant missions and research conditions.【Local script】【Local localisation】

Another branch sails toward Aelantir. The mission narrative acknowledges that the old colonial system extracted wealth from settlers' lands and sent it one way back to the Reach. The proposed reform turns colonies into autonomous league members while keeping commercial ties. This is not simply abandoning colonisation: Celmaldor still pursues sea lanes, tariffs, merchant networks, and economic influence over former colonies, but shifts from direct rule to cooperation and institutional links.【Local narrative text】

Domestic reform is also about more than trade modifiers. The Dran Act initially protects some human residents while leaving other humans and gnomes without equal rights. The future missions call for revising the Act to include more groups and redesigning elections that favour the capital and merchant families. Port recovery, merchant military power, overseas subjects, and civic rights converge on one question: does the republic enrich a small group of long-lived merchants, or do the cities and residents of the league benefit together?【Local narrative text】

Optional formation as The Reach, without a mission-tree swap

Celmaldor may form The Reach (B98) after meeting conditions including Blue Reach cities, administrative technology, and peace. This is optional and does not change the country's 1444 identity. The current exclusive mission group's potential accepts a B98 country that was previously Z22, so a Celmaldor that forms The Reach can continue this mission line. Completing “Human Rights” beforehand also enables an extra renaming effect in the formation decision. This B98 formation route should not be projected onto every Z22 campaign as an inevitable outcome.【Local script】

In play, secure the coast, build an army, and restore the port first; in the middle game, manage league members, northern markets, and artificer production; later, use overseas autonomy, legal reform, and a broad trade network to sustain expansion. It suits players who enjoy merchant republics, maritime economies, subject relations, and institutional change, not those who want to conquer neighbouring states rapidly with one land army. The official Dev Diary from 2025 explains the design context; current implementation remains governed by the local scripts.【Local script】【Official dev diary】

Personality is provisionally Expansion 75 | Autocracy 45 | Magic–Artifice direction 18 (intensity 83) | Pluralism 88; values are Good 76/100, improving. Unequal early rights, merchant private armies, and colonial extraction lower the initial assessment. Later legal expansion, overseas autonomy, and public works are positive evidence. The assessment does not award points automatically for being a trade republic or using liberation rhetoric, nor penalize overseas expansion by itself. Discussions whose version is unclear can illustrate that the mission chain and republican mechanics may take some interpretation, but do not establish an optimal current strategy.【Local narrative text】【Community view】 See the evidence record.

National Ideas (Reference Appendix)

The following reproduces current national traditions, seven national ideas and ambition. Traditions apply on adoption, ideas unlock through investment, and ambition follows completion of all seven. Only national ideas are listed, not racial, governmental or mission bonuses; predecessor and successor sets do not stack. Idea descriptions can recall history or describe future ideals and do not automatically establish events before 1444.

Effect displays and units are inherited for source parity, not independently certified; uncertain percentages remain accompanied by script keys and raw values.

Celmaldor (Z22) — Celmaldorian Ideas

Set ID: Z22_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = Z22
    }

Celmaldorian Traditions

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.1).

  • Global trade power: +10% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.1).

1. Maldorian the Navigator

Maldorian was a navigator-turned-captain of the Remnant Fleet who followed fellow navigator Munas Moonsinger to Cannor. However when they arrived Maldorian and his followers refused to join Munas and fight in the War of the Sorcerer-King, instead opting to lead his large migrant ship, the Whitespear, to the western fringes of the Alenic Reach, which was then largely populated by Alenic tribes.

There, the Moon Elves decided to found a settlement and make it their new home, where they could live without being embroiled in wars led by human kings. The city was named Celmaldor, meaning the "Harbor of Maldorian".

  • Range: +25% (range; raw value 0.25).

  • Light ship cost: -10% (light_ship_cost; raw value -0.1).

2. Elves of the Reach

We are Reachmen too! While elves who followed Munas became subjects and nobility of human kingdoms, we refused to give up our freedom to the rulers of human world. While we are sovereign over many humans, our elves haggle in the same markets as they do and do business with the same wares as they do. Here, in the Alenic Reach we have our small state which respects its independence. And independence of our Reachmen neighbors if they are ready to fight for it.

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

3. Icewind Palace of Commerce

Maldorian was a great leader, but mediocre ruler. He had little understanding of how diplomacy and trade worked, and was more accustomed to reading charts and sextants, eventually losing popularity amongst elven trade princes. One of the largest elven clans, the Icewinds, took power in their hands and started to develop the city as a northern centre of trade. They built a magnificent palace in Celmaldor's port, where Celmaldorian merchants gathered to discuss business and development of the city.

  • Number of merchants: +1 (merchants; raw value 1).

4. Delandian Act of Equality

Celmaldor grew rapidly, and its growth attracted attention from its neighbors, both good and bad. Gerudian raiders regularly attacked Celmaldorian ships and tried to pillage the city. The same problems were true for neighbouring cities, who were smaller and weaker than Celmaldor.

So, in order to fight this northern threat the cities of Deland and Mawdock asked Moon Elves to protect them in exchange for their independence and wealth. The trade princes agreed, and so a confederation, led by Celmaldor, was formed. Rights of human cities were listed in an act signed in Deland, and since then this document has been the basis for integration of all Reachmen city states, which looked for Celmaldorian protection.

  • Stability cost modifier: -10% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.1).

  • National unrest: -1 (global_unrest; raw value -1).

5. Escorts of the Trade Princes

Naturally long wars are devastating for elven countries. In its early years Celmaldor relied on levies from the neighbouring human tribes and militias from nearby towns, and for a time they tried (and failed) to form a standing army for the republic. Instead the many powerful trade princes of Celmaldor hire their own private armies that they loan to the state in times of war, these armies were often fully comprised of human mercenaries from all over the Reach, and for a time allowed Celmaldor relative security in their endeavours. Even when Celmaldor successfully funded their state armies comprised of elven elites, they were often supplemented by these so-called Escort Companies who were still majority human.

  • Manpower recovery speed: +15% (manpower_recovery_speed; raw value 0.15).

6. Sea is Our Land

As any other coastal city, Celmaldor relies heavily on control of the seas. It provides food, trade and wealth. But due to the legacy of the Remnant Fleet sea means even life to us, because without it our people would cease to exist. That is why our people mostly choose to connect their life with seas. And that is why our fleet should be feared.

  • Naval Morale: +15% (naval_morale; raw value 0.15).

7. Modern Elven Seamen

Its position at the exit of the Giant's Grave has made Celmaldor a prize for all seaborne conquerors of the northern seas.

Fending off the likes of Gerudians, gray orcs and gnomish hulks is each a worthy endevour in their own sakes, and as such the Celmaldorian navy had to modernize fast despite what was expected in their elven heritage. The ships of the Celmaldorian Navy were known to be fast and agile, and equipped with the latest cannons (despite what is said by elves and their reluctance to adopt new technologies) - and despite the navy's relatively small size in comparison with their rivals, they were known to go toe-to-toe from skirmishes in the open waters of Reaver's Sea to privateering whilst dodging in and out the many islands of the Frozen Pass.

  • Fleet movement speed modifier: +100% (Movement_speed_in_fleet_modifier; raw value 1).

  • Ship durability: +5% (Ship_durability; raw value 0.05).

Celmaldorian Ambition

  • Trade steering: +10% (trade_steering; raw value 0.1).

The Reach (B98) — Reachman Ideas

Set ID: B98_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B98
    }

Reachman Traditions

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).

  • Trade efficiency: +10% (trade_efficiency; raw value 0.10).

1. Men of the Reach

Reachman, a term first coined by the Castanorians and later introduced to Dameria via maps, was a slur. It referred to the barbarous and ignorant mix of Alenic and Gerudian peoples that sat along the coast, astride the edge of the world.

Then the Castanorians fell, and new peoples came. Some were of Castanor, others were more Gerudians or Alenics, and then others were newer arrivals; Gnomes from the storm Isles, elves led by the navigator Maldorian, and goblins escaping the horrors of Escann. And over time, it went from derogatory to congratulatory, offered to each new arrival as a welcome into the regional fold.

As we take the tentative steps into this new nation, 'Reachman' is a mark of pride and honor. It refers to those who have weathered the raging seas of the Giant’s Grave, those who brave the terrors of the Greatwoods, and those who do not kneel when outsiders claim us for their own.

  • Number of accepted cultures: +2 (num_accepted_cultures; raw value 2).

2. Standing Militia

The Reach is not a land of kings or conquerors but of wind and salt, of storm-wracked shores and deep forests where the world ends and the unknown begins. It is a land of those who endure—fisherfolk, shipwrights, hunters and herders, men and women who carve their lives out with their own two hands. We do not seek war, nor hunger for power. Yet we know that without defense, nothing is ours.

We take up arms not as soldiers, but as Reachmen. Our forces are not of conquest, but of defiance—a pledge that when invaders come, dockworker, forester, and merchant will fight as fiercely as any knight. When reavers darken our shores or foreign banners rise on our borders, they will find not helpless people, but a nation that fights as one.

The Battle of the Pier was their first lesson. The Grombari came, their commanders confident in swift victory. But there were no battle lines, no cities to sack, only a land that would not be taken. For three days, they marched and were met with only shadows and steel. The forests swallowed their scouts. The roads led them into ambush. The tides turned red with their retreat. By the third day, they fled, not before an army, but before a people who would never bow.

  • Reinforce speed: +15% (reinforce_speed; raw value 0.15).

3. Imperishablism

Imperishablism was envisioned by Ardoor Green, a kids fable writer, as the future of the Reach. He dreamed of an interconnected urban expanse spanning the entire region, a single, unified city that would stand against time and turmoil: Alvic, 'the all vic'. Scholars and planners, drawing from traditions of urban construction from across Halcann, believed that only by reshaping the land itself could the Reach secure its future. Though the dream of a fully realized Alvic never came to pass, its principles reshaped the cities of the Reach forever.

Instead of focusing on a singular, central metropolis, Imperishablist rulers and civic engineers pursued vast urban renewal projects—dykes and dams to tame the tides, land reclamation efforts to expand settlements, and new infrastructure linking cities like never before. By the end of the magnate uprising, roads and canals bound the Reach together, while fortified harbors and elevated districts stood resilient against the region’s many threats.

Though the grand vision remains unfinished, its impact is undeniable. The Reach may not have become one city, but it has become one nation, stronger, more connected, and built to endure.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.10).

4. Prosperity-Effort Ethic

The Reach has always been a land of traders, merchants, and builders. Yet for centuries, the wealth of the Reach merely circled its competing cities, never truly benefiting Reachman independence. That changed with the words of Taelar Hare, a Corinite follower of Ara who built upon the teachings of Aucan Órdimair. He argued that wealth was not a vice nor a test, but a gift – one that, when shared and cultivated, was a mark of divine favor.

The Reach listened. Temples became more than places of worship; they became centers of commerce, housing stock exchanges where faith and finance intertwined. Markets grew, paper money spread, and trade flourished like never before. In time, this doctrine reshaped the Reach into a society of capital, where prosperity was not just an ambition, but a calling.

The gods bless those who build, who trade, who bring fortune to their kin. And in the Reach, wealth is no longer just measured in gold—it is measured in paper, in ones faith in their fellows, in innovation and ingenuity, and in boundless opportunities seized.

  • Goods produced modifier: +10% (global_trade_goods_size_modifier; raw value 0.10).

  • Clergy loyalty equilibrium: +5% (church_loyalty_modifier; raw value 0.05).

5. The Reachgard

With the fall of the Second Reign of Adshaw, foreign powers, especially Gawedi Magnates, moved to dominate the Reach’s trade. In response, domestic Magnates founded the Reach Naval Committee, an independent organization focused on subsidizing ports, coordinating naval trade, and securing economic autonomy from outside rule.

One of its first actions was the creation of the Reachgard, a marine and police force tasked with protecting commerce from exploitation. The Reachgard patrolled trade routes, cracked down on foreign monopolies, and resisted unjust policies imposed by their new rulers. By taking control of their own maritime security, the Reach ensured that its prosperity would no longer be dictated by outside forces.

  • Naval Force Limit Modifier: +15% (naval_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.15).

  • Marine force limit: +25% (allowed_marine_fraction; raw value 0.25).

6. Kaupor Headquarters

The Reach has never relied on military expansion, instead using economic influence as its greatest weapon. One of the most effective tools in this strategy is the institution of the Kaupor - 'market town' in Gerudian. These free trade zones, established within foreign nations, allow Reach merchants to operate with minimal restrictions, expanding the region’s influence without the need for force.

By securing favorable trade agreements and embedding themselves within key markets, the Reach strengthens its diplomatic ties while ensuring that its wealth flows beyond its borders. Kaupor Headquarters oversee these operations, coordinating commercial efforts and securing economic footholds in foreign lands.

  • Diplomatic relations: +1 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 1).

  • Reduced trade penalty outside the main trade node: +25% (reduced_trade_penalty_on_non_main_tradenode; raw value 0.25).

7. The Last Blue League

For generations, efforts to unite the Reachmen failed, shattered by distance, by pride, and by the weight of outside rule. But during the Magnate Uprising, something changed. The Reach no longer asked for unity. It demanded it.

From this spark, the Ragnian Commonwealth was born—forged in the fires of the chaotic Ordal Compromise, carried by voices who cried for liberty from Gawed. Factionalism plagued it, yes, but still it stood: the first true government built by Reachmen, for Reachmen.

They called it the Last Blue League—a final effort to bind the Western Reach together not through conquest, but through shared purpose: freedom, safety, and progress. It was not perfect, but it was ours.

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

Reachman Ambitions

  • Naval Morale: +10% (naval_morale; raw value 0.10).
